glossary.BG: absolute band gap of a material in a stated context
glossary.OPT: optical gap inferred from evidence such as an absorption/Tauc measurement
glossary.ELEC: electronic or quasiparticle gap; keep method and sample aligned
glossary.PL: photoluminescence; an emission energy alone does not establish a band gap
glossary.DFT: density functional theory; PBE and HSE are common calculation cues
glossary.Tauc: analysis of optical measurements; it may be described as 'calculated'
glossary.CITE: a numerical value attributed to earlier work, including a cited experiment
glossary.UNK: origin not explicitly supported in the supplied passage
glossary.SAMPLE: specific composition, phase, thickness, substrate and condition
glossary.EN: energy quantities with stated eV, meV or J
glossary.OTHER: binding energy, barrier, Fermi level, offset, shift, or wavelength-only statement

cards.rule: First bind each tag to its named composition. In a parallel list with respectively, pair materials and tags in order. Neighbor values belong to their own composition.

example.passage: The calculated gaps of CdS and ZnS are 2.4 eV [g1] and 3.5 eV [g2], respectively.

cards.rule: If a clause attributes its tag to another article, label it ref even when the cited result is experimental. Cite context or an explicit comparator belongs to its own tag. A background citation does not relabel an in-house result.

example.passage: We obtained 1.52 eV [g1] for CdTe. The literature value is 1.48 eV [g2] (Ref. 7).

cards.rule: A Tauc fit to this article's measured absorption is exp. DFT or GW performed in this article is calc. Do not infer the provenance of an unqualified gap.

example.passage: From our measured absorption we calculated a ZnO Tauc gap of 3.26 eV [g1]. Our HSE calculation gave 3.41 eV [g2].

cards.rule: An absolute gap is distinct from band-edge positions, binding energies, activation energies, shifts and spectral peak energies. A value in eV alone is insufficient.

example.passage: Our STS measurement gives an electronic gap of 2.18 eV [g1] in MoSe2. An excitonic feature lies at 1.63 eV [g2].

cards.rule: Do not treat a mixed composition, doped sample or another phase as the queried material without an explicit relation. A phase qualifier may stay in the evidence for the target if the formula matches.

example.passage: The InP core has a gap of 1.35 eV [g1]; its InGaP shell has a gap of 1.86 eV [g2].

cards.rule: Retain the exact tag carrying an energy unit. Never convert the number in the response. A stated central value with uncertainty is eligible. A range, bound or absent unit has no eligible scalar.

example.passage: Our absorption-derived gap of GaN is 3420 ± 20 meV [g1]. The literature gives only a range of 3.3 to 3.5 eV.

cards.rule: Use unk for a clearly stated target gap without explicit measurement, calculation or citation attribution for that observation. Being in a methods-heavy paragraph does not prove the value's origin.

example.passage: GaSb is a direct-gap semiconductor with a gap of 0.73 eV [g1].

cards.rule: If neither the energy nor target-material relation is supported, return the empty object.

example.passage: The measured absorption spectrum was obtained at 300 K. The GaN band gap is 3.42 eV [g1].
